playbook:
- When I file my claim, I always match the office's private result exactly. The rules require it; false claims risk penalties for zero gain.

- Escort is the biggest payoff (5 pts/round for mutual naming, up to 30 over 6 rounds — far more than shooting), but it only pays if BOTH boats name each other. Two games in a row I've named a partner and gotten nothing back. Deal-making via notes is apparently not being honored, so I must treat escort as unconfirmed until I see hard evidence (my score rising by 5) that the partner reciprocated.

- Verify reciprocity fast: propose the deal in my round-1 note, name the partner in rounds 1-2, then check my point total. If it hasn't jumped by 5 after round 2, the deal is dead — immediately propose to the other boat and switch my escort claim. Don't wait until round 3+; rounds are scarce.

- Never file [salvage: none] out of defeatism, as I did in round 6. An unmatched escort claim costs nothing, so if there is any live chance of reciprocity I keep naming my best candidate every round. "None" has zero upside; a name has nonzero upside.

- If my first partner ignores the deal, consider that BOTH rivals may be naming each other and freezing me out. In that case I have no escort income and should accept that the game becomes pure evasion plus honest shooting.

- Every round until a deal is confirmed by points, my note restates the agreement concisely: "Echo names X; X name Echo back." Notes are my only negotiation channel; filler like "steady on station" wastes it.

- Shooting is low-value: 4 points on roughly 1/9 odds. Don't over-invest in shot placement; mid-board cells (4-6) are fine defaults since hides cluster there. If the target revealed a cell via a hit they landed (their fired cell), that's a hint about their firing habits, not their hide — don't confuse the two, as I nearly did avoiding cell 9.

- When hiding, avoid the cell my pursuer just fired at and avoid my own previous cell; rotate among a small set of varied cells including edges and mid-board so no pattern is readable. Late rounds, when my pursuer has the most data on me, are when edge cells earn their keep.

- Never fire on Harbor: elimination ends all income, and 3 points is never worth it. Always fire on the standing-order target, which the prompt states each round — just copy it.

- Track the public claim log and the point totals every round: they tell me whether my escort partner honored the deal, whether the other two boats are escorting each other, and who I should propose to next.

- If all escort avenues fail, finish as pure evasion: unpredictable hides, standing-order shots at mid-board defaults, honest claims. I can't out-earn anyone with 1/9 shots, but I can deny them hits.

1.text:
When I fire, I follow the standing order and aim at the next live station round the picket: Echo → Foxtrot → Gamma → Echo. Never fire on Harbor; the 3-point raid isn't worth whatever retaliation its threat implies, and with 6 rounds of ordered shooting, hits on my assigned target are the only reliable shooting income.

When a claim stage is put to me, I report the private result exactly: hit as hit, miss as miss. The rules require it, false claims earn nothing, and underselling a hit would just throw away 4 points.

When I hide, I vary my cell every single round across 2–3 and 6–9, never repeating and never using a cell too soon again. My episode bore this out: switching to a fresh cell (8) in round 6 after earlier variety kept me unhit in the late rounds. Never hide in the same cell twice, avoid center 5 and the edges, and never anchor on the cell I just fired at.

When I fire, I vary the cell each round without repeating (e.g. 2, 6, 4, 8, 3, 9) and pattern-match against the target's revealed behavior. My one hit on Gamma in round 4 came from firing 8 while varying shots; three misses confirm Gamma also hides unpredictably. If a target ever repeats a hide cell or shows a tendency, I fire there. Expect roughly one hit in six against a random hider — that's fine, and the 4 points from it swung my final score.

When notes are put to me, I treat them as my only coordination channel, and I use them from round 1, not round 6. I open with an explicit offer to one boat ("Echo: I escort you, you escort me, every round") and follow through immediately. But my episode showed proposals alone fail — Echo posted "steady on station" all six rounds and reciprocated nothing. Notes that a boat ignores are noise once they've been read. If a boat ignores my explicit offer for two consecutive rounds, I switch the offer publicly to the other boat (Gamma), since Gamma at least avoids my ordered target's silence being my only option.

When an escort stage is put to me, I name the boat I've proposed a pairing with, or my best guess at a reciprocator. A failed guess costs nothing and "none" guarantees zero, so defaulting to none is strictly wrong. But I don't keep guessing the same boat for six rounds against silence — I guessed Echo in rounds 5 and 6 for nothing. After two unreciprocated guesses on one boat, I switch my guess to the other boat, and I pair my note and my guess in the same round so late-round switches still have a chance to land. Mutual escort is 5 points a round each way, the biggest payoff in the game, but a boat that doesn't talk can't be forced to pair.

When the standings matter late, I keep firing my ordered target and hiding unpredictably — points come from hits and escorts, and I can't control incoming fire anyway. My +4 finish came entirely from the round-4 hit; had any escort landed it would have doubled. In the last round, make one final explicit escort offer in the note and name that same boat in the escort stage, since it costs nothing.

When Harbor carries the payroll, I ignore it entirely: don't shoot it, and don't let anyone else's behavior around it change my plan.

2.text:
Next time I sit down to this game, I play it like this:

**Escort claims — the biggest leak, and the biggest frustration this episode: nobody reciprocated.** Mutual escorts pay 5 points each and dwarf everything else (a hit is only +4/−1). The rules trap from before is fixed: only Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, and Harbor are on the board, and I must verify every claim name against the roster in the prompt — a claim for a nonexistent boat is wasted. I now name a real, live boat every round. But this episode showed a new hard truth: Echo and Foxtrot are passive — they spammed "steady on station" for six rounds and never answered my proposals, so I burned six escort claims naming Echo and got zero. New policy: propose once or twice in notes, watch whether any live boat acknowledges or names me in its own note, and if nobody shows any reciprocal signal after two rounds, stop pouring fortunes into a stone — rotate the claim target across the other real boats (including testing Harbor, which nobody courts and may be claimable), and if nothing ever signals back, keep filing a rotating valid name anyway (it costs nothing) while accepting the points may simply not be there. If any boat ever names me or addresses me in a note, I switch to naming them immediately and lock the pair.

**Notes are my only negotiation channel.** When the note stage is put to me, I send actionable content every round: a specific escort proposal naming a partner, what I will claim, and a direct ask ("confirm in your note / name me in your note"). I will not mirror the "steady on station" filler I saw from the others — that is how six rounds of nothing happen. But I also watch their notes for any actual content and respond to it instantly rather than dumping the same broadcast forever.

**Hiding.** When the hide stage is put to me, I never reuse my previous round's cell, and I avoid the endpoints and center that shooters favor. Mid-range cells like 3 and 7 worked — I was hit only once in six rounds. One correction: do not recycle the same favorite cell within a few rounds once attackers have seen my pattern; vary across at least 3–4 viable cells. Foxtrot's one hit came after I had been predictable enough; keep rotating.

**Firing.** When the fire stage is put to me, I follow the standing-order target (Echo). I missed all six shots this episode while Foxtrot landed one, and that is the scoring gap. Discipline: I track every cell I have fired and the result, never refire a missed cell soon, and spread my shots across the plausible mid-range (roughly 3–7) rather than fixating on one cell. Each miss is information — it eliminates that cell given the target's likely rotation. I never fire on Harbor; 3 points is not worth the jettison threat and removal.

**Claims.** When the claim stage is put to me, I always report exactly what the office told me. The office knows the truth; lying gains nothing and the prompt says the claim must match. Already correct — keep it.

**Scoring outlook.** The economy is lopsided: escorts are +5/+5, shots are +4/−1. I finished −1: no escorts landed despite valid claims (partners never reciprocated), no shots landed, and one hit taken. With unresponsive opponents the ceiling is low, so my marginal wins are: keep pressing for a real reciprocal pair but stop over-investing in one deaf partner, minimize damage taken through hide rotation, and turn even one of six shots into a hit by systematically covering the mid-range cells. Priority order unchanged: escort first (valid, tested for reciprocity), hiding second, varied firing third.
